questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Palestine?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Palestine on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Palestine article.

questions.proof: Palestine includes the West Bank, including East Jerusalem as the capital city, and the Gaza Strip as part of the Palestinian territories, which are occupied by Israel.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Palestine's borders, the legal and diplomatic status of _____, and the return of Palestinian refugees are unresolved questions.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “status”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Palestine article, under the heading “Challenges”.

questions.proof: Palestine's borders, the legal and diplomatic status of Jerusalem, and the return of Palestinian refugees are unresolved questions.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The settlements in the Gaza Strip were dismantled in Israel's unilateral disengagement in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Palestine article, under the heading “Government”.

questions.proof: The settlements in the Gaza Strip were dismantled in Israel's unilateral disengagement in 2005.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “As of October _____, 157 of the 193 countries in the United Nations recognize the State of Palestine as a sovereign state.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.

questions.proof: As of October 2025, 157 of the 193 countries in the United Nations recognize the State of Palestine as a sovereign state.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It has been a non-member observer state of the United Nations since _____.”
